facts.text: ブラウザのHTTP通信を途中で書き換えたり、モック（偽の応答）にしたりする開発者向けのオープンソースツール。画面側の開発者が、バックエンド担当のAPI完成待ちや、不安定なバックエンドに作業を止められる問題に応える。
創業者Sachin Jainは、本番環境の圧縮されたJavaScriptをデバッグしたいという苛立ちから、約30分でChrome拡張の最初の版を作った。Baremetricsの紹介文は、週末の個人制作から始まったと説明する。

2018年、JavaScriptファイルを差し替えるだけの道具として始まった。変更を試すためだけに配備し直す手間を省く道具で、のちにコンテンツセキュリティポリシーに当たった開発者向けにHTTPヘッダーの書き換えも加わった。デスクトップ型の傍受ツールと違い、ブラウザの機能で通信を傍受するため、システム全体のプロキシ設定や証明書の導入が要らず、会社のVPNでも動く。その後、チームで設定を共有する機能が加わった。
Sachin Jainは共同創業者でCEO。Baremetricsの紹介文によれば、Googleのインターンとアドビのエンジニアを経て起業した。
チームは、API応答の偽装（モック）が最も製品に合っていると見て、バックエンドの完成待ちから画面側の開発者を解放する方向へ軸足を移した。企業向けにはSSO、SLA、分析と報告、役割別の権限管理、SOC2 Type II認証を足した。
Baremetricsの紹介文によれば、Requestlyは約1万7千件の応募から採択された414社の1社としてY Combinatorに入った。
Baremetricsの対談の紹介文は、ランディングページやマーケティングに頼らず自然に広まり、Stack OverflowとGitHubが販売戦略のすべてだったと説明する。
収益化では、純粋な収益化よりオープンコアモデルを選んだ。
発表は、RequestlyがY Combinator、Peak XV（旧Sequoia）、複数の著名エンジェルの出資を受けたと書く。
2025年5月6日、BrowserStackがRequestlyの買収を発表した。発表は、Requestlyを独立したオープンソースの道具として続け、今後はモバイル端末やシミュレータ向けの傍受・モック機能を出す計画としている。
発表によれば、買収時のRequestlyは20万人超の開発者、1万社超の企業が使い、Chromeストアの評価は1,200件超のレビューで4.3。Sachin Jainは、環境とバックエンド担当への依存でコードの通しテストが止まる無駄な開発時間への苛立ちから生まれたと述べている。
売り先の選び方について、創業者は価格より適した買い手を優先する考え方を語っている。
料金ページはAPI PlatformのTeamを年払いで1利用者あたり月換算$10、Team Proを$15と表示する。
公式の製品ページは、通信を書き換えるルール機能、APIクライアント、モックサーバー、チーム共有、暗号化した秘密情報の保管、自動テストを並べ、30万人超の開発者に使われているとうたう。

Home Press BrowserStack Acquires Requestly, a YCombinator Startup for HTTP Interception, Mocking & Debugging Network Requests BrowserStack Acquires Requestly, a YCombinator Startup for HTTP Interception, Mocking & Debugging Network Requests
Strategic acquisition addresses critical bottlenecks in modern web development through advanced HTTP interception, debugging, and mocking of network requests.
DUBLIN—May 6, 2025 — BrowserStack today announced the acquisition of Requestly , the popular open-source HTTP interception and API mocking tool that eliminates critical bottlenecks in modern web development. This strategic acquisition strengthens BrowserStack’s commitment to developer productivity by supporting Requestly’s growth as a beloved HTTP interception and mocking solution, providing developers with tools that significantly accelerate their workflow.
Frontend developers consistently face two major obstacles that derail productivity and delay releases: dependency on backend developers to complete APIs before frontend work can progress, and unreliable backend services during development and testing.
These challenges manifest as blocked sprints, delayed releases, and frustrated developer experiences when backend teams are still building needed endpoints or APIs don’t return data required for development.
Requestly directly addresses these pain points through its browser-based approach to intercept and mock network requests:
Shift-left development experience : Delivers faster web development by offering comprehensive tools for HTTP interception, debugging, and mocking, supporting use cases from cloud-based mocking to JS redirects and local testing.
Zero-configuration setup : It installs directly into the browser and uses browser APIs to intercept and modify requests, eliminating the need to manage system-level proxy settings and install SSL certificates. This ensures it works well with corporate VPNs.
Open-source, secure, and enterprise-read y: Requestly is an open-source solution providing flexibility and speed for web development. For enterprises, Requestly provides features like SSO, SLAs, SOC-II compliance, reporting and analytics, and role-based access control for efficient management.
Seamless workflow integration : Built primarily as a browser extension with a minimalistic and intuitive design, requiring no learning curve for developers.
Team collaboration : Enables teams to organize and collaborate on projects effectively through shared workspaces where users can instantly share rules, environments, and mocks.
Requestly has achieved remarkable adoption among developers worldwide, trusted by 200,000+ developers from 10,000+ companies, ranging from Fortune 500 to startups. The tool maintains a Chrome Store rating of 4.3 from 1200+ reviews and has a growing open-source community with active contributors. As a YCombinator graduate and a part of Peak XV (formerly Sequoia) Surge, Requestly has established itself as a leading solution for interception, debugging, and mocking of HTTP requests.
“Requestly was born from our own frustration of wasted developer hours due to broken workflows in end-to-end code testing caused by dependency on the environment & backend team,” said Sachin Jain, Founder of Requestly. “Joining BrowserStack means we can maintain our core values while accelerating our roadmap to address even more developer pain points. Our community will benefit from increased investment while we remain true to our vision and open-source roots.”
“What drew us to Requestly was its innovative browser-native approach and the passionate developer community behind it,” said Ritesh Arora, CEO & Co-founder of BrowserStack. “We’re excited to accelerate Requestly’s disruption of the API mocking and interception space while preserving its open-source foundation. We’re backing Requestly’s growth while maintaining what developers love about it—this will help them innovate faster in a space ready for fresh thinking.”
Requestly’s evolution mirrors the changing needs of modern web development. What began in 2018 as a simple tool to redirect JavaScript files for local testing has transformed into a comprehensive HTTP Interception & Mocking tool trusted by hundreds of thousands of developers.
Initially, solving the frustration of deploying JavaScript changes just to test them, Requestly expanded to handle HTTP header modifications when developers faced Content Security Policy challenges. Taking a revolutionary Chrome-Extension based approach to HTTP interception—unlike traditional desktop-based proxy solutions—Requestly developed capabilities to intercept and modify all HTTP requests, positioning it as a lightweight alternative to complex proxy tools.
The addition of team workspaces enabled seamless developer collaboration through shared configurations. As mobile development has expanded, Requestly plans to support Android emulators and iOS simulators in upcoming releases.
Recognizing that API mocking represented Requestly’s strongest product-market fit, the team refocused on helping developers work independently from backend dependencies. Enterprise features like SOC2 Type II certification followed, culminating in a comprehensive network interception & mocking tool. Throughout this journey, Requestly has remained true to its open-source roots while continuously adapting to meet developers’ evolving needs.
BrowserStack emphasized its commitment to maintaining Requestly as an independent, open-source tool, ensuring the developer community continues to benefit from its accessibility and flexibility. The future roadmap includes launching HTTP interception and mocking capabilities for mobile devices and simulators.
Requestly continues to be available as an open-source tool, now backed by BrowserStack’s resources and commitment to developer productivity. Developers can download the extension from the Chrome Web Store or as a Mac App here .

This week we sit down with Sachin Jain, Co-founder and CEO of Requestly. You'll hear about turning a 30-minute hack into a YC-backed developer tool, why he chose the open core model over pure monetization, how Stack Overflow and GitHub became their entire GTM strategy, and the acquisition framework that prioritizes the right buyer over the right price.
About Sachin Jain:
Sachin Jain is the Co-founder and CEO of Requestly, the browser-based API mocking and testing platform used by over 300,000 developers worldwide. After transforming a weekend Chrome extension project into a Y Combinator-backed company (one of 414 accepted from 17,000 applications), Sachin led Requestly through a successful acquisition by BrowserStack earlier this year. His journey from Google intern and Adobe engineer to successful founder showcases the power of solving your own problems first.
About Requestly:
Requestly is a developer-first platform that simplifies API mocking, testing, and network request interception directly in the browser. Born from a frustrated developer's need to debug minified JavaScript in production, Requestly eliminates the need for bulky proxy tools by offering a simple Chrome extension that lets developers modify headers, redirect scripts, and mock API responses. The platform has become essential for frontend teams building against incomplete backends.

facts.text: ブラウザのHTTP通信を途中で書き換えたり、モック（偽の応答）にしたりする開発者向けのオープンソースツール。画面側の開発者が、バックエンド担当のAPI完成待ちや、不安定なバックエンドに作業を止められる問題に応える。
創業者Sachin Jainは、本番環境の圧縮されたJavaScriptをデバッグしたいという苛立ちから、約30分でChrome拡張の最初の版を作った。Baremetricsの紹介文は、週末の個人制作から始まったと説明する。

2018年、JavaScriptファイルを差し替えるだけの道具として始まった。変更を試すためだけに配備し直す手間を省く道具で、のちにコンテンツセキュリティポリシーに当たった開発者向けにHTTPヘッダーの書き換えも加わった。デスクトップ型の傍受ツールと違い、ブラウザの機能で通信を傍受するため、システム全体のプロキシ設定や証明書の導入が要らず、会社のVPNでも動く。その後、チームで設定を共有する機能が加わった。
Sachin Jainは共同創業者でCEO。Baremetricsの紹介文によれば、Googleのインターンとアドビのエンジニアを経て起業した。
チームは、API応答の偽装（モック）が最も製品に合っていると見て、バックエンドの完成待ちから画面側の開発者を解放する方向へ軸足を移した。企業向けにはSSO、SLA、分析と報告、役割別の権限管理、SOC2 Type II認証を足した。
Baremetricsの紹介文によれば、Requestlyは約1万7千件の応募から採択された414社の1社としてY Combinatorに入った。
Baremetricsの対談の紹介文は、ランディングページやマーケティングに頼らず自然に広まり、Stack OverflowとGitHubが販売戦略のすべてだったと説明する。
収益化では、純粋な収益化よりオープンコアモデルを選んだ。
発表は、RequestlyがY Combinator、Peak XV（旧Sequoia）、複数の著名エンジェルの出資を受けたと書く。
2025年5月6日、BrowserStackがRequestlyの買収を発表した。発表は、Requestlyを独立したオープンソースの道具として続け、今後はモバイル端末やシミュレータ向けの傍受・モック機能を出す計画としている。
発表によれば、買収時のRequestlyは20万人超の開発者、1万社超の企業が使い、Chromeストアの評価は1,200件超のレビューで4.3。Sachin Jainは、環境とバックエンド担当への依存でコードの通しテストが止まる無駄な開発時間への苛立ちから生まれたと述べている。
売り先の選び方について、創業者は価格より適した買い手を優先する考え方を語っている。
料金ページはAPI PlatformのTeamを年払いで1利用者あたり月換算$10、Team Proを$15と表示する。
公式の製品ページは、通信を書き換えるルール機能、APIクライアント、モックサーバー、チーム共有、暗号化した秘密情報の保管、自動テストを並べ、30万人超の開発者に使われているとうたう。

Strategic acquisition addresses critical bottlenecks in modern web development through advanced HTTP interception, debugging, and mocking of network requests.
DUBLIN—May 6, 2025 — BrowserStack today announced the acquisition of Requestly , the popular open-source HTTP interception and API mocking tool that eliminates critical bottlenecks in modern web development. This strategic acquisition strengthens BrowserStack’s commitment to developer productivity by supporting Requestly’s growth as a beloved HTTP interception and mocking solution, providing developers with tools that significantly accelerate their workflow.
Frontend developers consistently face two major obstacles that derail productivity and delay releases: dependency on backend developers to complete APIs before frontend work can progress, and unreliable backend services during development and testing.
These challenges manifest as blocked sprints, delayed releases, and frustrated developer experiences when backend teams are still building needed endpoints or APIs don’t return data required for development.
Requestly directly addresses these pain points through its browser-based approach to intercept and mock network requests:
Shift-left development experience : Delivers faster web development by offering comprehensive tools for HTTP interception, debugging, and mocking, supporting use cases from cloud-based mocking to JS redirects and local testing.
Zero-configuration setup : It installs directly into the browser and uses browser APIs to intercept and modify requests, eliminating the need to manage system-level proxy settings and install SSL certificates. This ensures it works well with corporate VPNs.
Open-source, secure, and enterprise-read y: Requestly is an open-source solution providing flexibility and speed for web development. For enterprises, Requestly provides features like SSO, SLAs, SOC-II compliance, reporting and analytics, and role-based access control for efficient management.
Seamless workflow integration : Built primarily as a browser extension with a minimalistic and intuitive design, requiring no learning curve for developers.
Team collaboration : Enables teams to organize and collaborate on projects effectively through shared workspaces where users can instantly share rules, environments, and mocks.
Requestly has achieved remarkable adoption among developers worldwide, trusted by 200,000+ developers from 10,000+ companies, ranging from Fortune 500 to startups. The tool maintains a Chrome Store rating of 4.3 from 1200+ reviews and has a growing open-source community with active contributors. As a YCombinator graduate and a part of Peak XV (formerly Sequoia) Surge, Requestly has established itself as a leading solution for interception, debugging, and mocking of HTTP requests.
“Requestly was born from our own frustration of wasted developer hours due to broken workflows in end-to-end code testing caused by dependency on the environment & backend team,” said Sachin Jain, Founder of Requestly. “Joining BrowserStack means we can maintain our core values while accelerating our roadmap to address even more developer pain points. Our community will benefit from increased investment while we remain true to our vision and open-source roots.”
“What drew us to Requestly was its innovative browser-native approach and the passionate developer community behind it,” said Ritesh Arora, CEO & Co-founder of BrowserStack. “We’re excited to accelerate Requestly’s disruption of the API mocking and interception space while preserving its open-source foundation. We’re backing Requestly’s growth while maintaining what developers love about it—this will help them innovate faster in a space ready for fresh thinking.”
Requestly’s evolution mirrors the changing needs of modern web development. What began in 2018 as a simple tool to redirect JavaScript files for local testing has transformed into a comprehensive HTTP Interception & Mocking tool trusted by hundreds of thousands of developers.
Initially, solving the frustration of deploying JavaScript changes just to test them, Requestly expanded to handle HTTP header modifications when developers faced Content Security Policy challenges. Taking a revolutionary Chrome-Extension based approach to HTTP interception—unlike traditional desktop-based proxy solutions—Requestly developed capabilities to intercept and modify all HTTP requests, positioning it as a lightweight alternative to complex proxy tools.
The addition of team workspaces enabled seamless developer collaboration through shared configurations. As mobile development has expanded, Requestly plans to support Android emulators and iOS simulators in upcoming releases.
Recognizing that API mocking represented Requestly’s strongest product-market fit, the team refocused on helping developers work independently from backend dependencies. Enterprise features like SOC2 Type II certification followed, culminating in a comprehensive network interception & mocking tool. Throughout this journey, Requestly has remained true to its open-source roots while continuously adapting to meet developers’ evolving needs.
BrowserStack emphasized its commitment to maintaining Requestly as an independent, open-source tool, ensuring the developer community continues to benefit from its accessibility and flexibility. The future roadmap includes launching HTTP interception and mocking capabilities for mobile devices and simulators.
Requestly continues to be available as an open-source tool, now backed by BrowserStack’s resources and commitment to developer productivity. Developers can download the extension from the Chrome Web Store or as a Mac App here .

BrowserStack is the world’s leading software testing platform, powering over two million tests every day across 19 global data centers. BrowserStack helps Amazon, NVIDIA, MongoDB, Microsoft, X, and over 50,000 customers deliver quality software at speed by moving testing to their Cloud. About Sachin Jain:
Sachin Jain is the Co-founder and CEO of Requestly, the browser-based API mocking and testing platform used by over 300,000 developers worldwide. After transforming a weekend Chrome extension project into a Y Combinator-backed company (one of 414 accepted from 17,000 applications), Sachin led Requestly through a successful acquisition by BrowserStack earlier this year. His journey from Google intern and Adobe engineer to successful founder showcases the power of solving your own problems first.
About Requestly:
Requestly is a developer-first platform that simplifies API mocking, testing, and network request interception directly in the browser. Born from a frustrated developer's need to debug minified JavaScript in production, Requestly eliminates the need for bulky proxy tools by offering a simple Chrome extension that lets developers modify headers, redirect scripts, and mock API responses. The platform has become essential for frontend teams building against incomplete backends.

Core API Client
REST, GraphQL & SOAP composers Dedicated request composers for REST, GraphQL and SOAP, each with the body, header and query editors that protocol needs.
WebSocket, gRPC & MQTT (build, send & run) Build, send and run realtime and streaming protocols — WebSocket, Socket.IO, gRPC and MQTT — alongside your HTTP requests.
Code-snippet generation Generate a ready-to-paste client snippet for any request, in the language and library your team already uses.
Cookie jar A per-domain cookie store that persists across requests, so authenticated session flows behave as they do in a browser.
Import & migration (Postman, Insomnia, Bruno) Bring collections and variables across from Postman, OpenAPI, HAR, cURL, WSDL, SoapUI or Bruno. Existing test scripts run without a rewrite.
Export & backup Export any collection or project to a portable file at any time, so your work is never locked in.
Collections & environment
Collections & folders Group related requests into collections and nested folders that mirror how your APIs are organised.
Request history & search Every request you send is retained and searchable, so you can find and replay a past call.
Variables & scoping Define variables at global, project, environment and request scope, with the nearest scope winning.
Auth & secrets
Advanced Auth types (API key / Bearer / Basic, OAuth 1/2, JWT, NTLM) All auth helpers — API key, Bearer, Basic, OAuth 1.0 & 2.0, JWT and NTLM — configured per request, folder or collection.
AWS SigV4 request signing Signature Version 4 for calling AWS APIs and other SigV4-protected endpoints.
mTLS / client & CA certificates Client certificates and custom CA bundles for mutual-TLS endpoints.
Vault & secret managers
Local vault An encrypted local vault that keeps credentials on your own machine and out of collection files.
External vault integrations (HashiCorp, Azure, 1Password) Securely pull secrets from HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault and 1Password integrations.
Secret scanner Detect potential secrets in API requests and elements against unwanted sharing or syncing.
Scripting, testing & automation
Pre/post-request scripts Run JavaScript before a request or after the response arrives, to set up state or assert on results.
Assertions & no-code test builder Write assertions in script or visually without code from a guided editor.
Collection runner (unlimited) Run a whole collection locally as often as you need — runs are not metered and carry no credit cap.
CLI runner Run the same collections in terminal or CI agent using the Requestly CLI.
CI/CD integration Wire collection runs into your pipeline to gate a build like any other test suite.
Data-driven testing Drive one request over data supplied from a file, producing a result per row.
Scheduled cloud runs Run collections on a schedule without keeping a machine of your own left running.
Reusable script library Share helper functions and snippets across requests and collections instead of copying script between them.
Basic test-result history Retain the results of recent runs to inspect what passed and what failed.
Advanced Test Reporting & Analytics Test reports, exportable execution trends over time, integrated with Test Reporting & Analytics.
Mock servers
Mock servers (generated from a collection) Spin up a mock server rapidly from a collection, to unblock front-end and mobile teams while the API is still in progress.
Dynamic / stateful mocks Mocks that vary their response by request content and remember state across calls, rather than replaying one fixed payload.
Collaboration & projects
Team projects Cloud-backed projects where collections, environments and history are shared with your team in realtime.
Shared team environments with secret masking Share environments across the team while keeping secret values masked from members who should not read them.
Shared / managed package library A managed library of shared script packages, available to every project in the organisation.
Comments & mentions Discuss a request or spec in place, and pull a teammate in with an @mention.
Activity Logs A feed of who changed what, and when, across the project.
Local Projects Projects that live on your own machine, giving you complete control over your data, with full native Git workflows.
Version Control (Local projects only) Full version control for Local Projects, backed by Git and working the way your code repository does.
2-way Git sync Push and pull collection changes to GitHub or GitLab, so API changes follow the same review and branching workflow as code.
Branching, forking & pull requests Branch or fork a collection, then merge it back through a pull request.
Merge & conflict resolution Resolve conflicting edits to the same request or collection through a guided merge.
Diff view See exactly what changed between two versions of a collection, request or spec.
AI Suite
AI test / assertion generation Generate tests and assertions for a request from its schema and its past responses.
AI-assisted debugging & error resolution Explain a failing request or response, and suggest the fix.
AI assistant An in-app assistant that answers questions about your APIs and carries out work in the client.
MCP server (upcoming) Expose your APIs and collections to AI IDEs and agents over the Model Context Protocol.

Schema ↔ collection sync Keep an OpenAPI spec and the collection generated from it in step, in both directions.
Schema versioning Version and release specs, so consumers can pin to a known revision.
Design Governance rules Auto-enforced API design and governance rules, applied as specs are authored.
Auto-generated hosted docs Documentation generated from the spec and hosted for you, refreshed on each release.
Embeddable docs Embed the generated documentation in your own site or developer portal.

Advanced / attribute-based RBAC Fine-grained, attribute-based roles and permissions, beyond the standard member roles.
Audit logs + SIEM export A tamper-evident audit trail of platform activity, exportable to your SIEM.
Data residency / self-hosting Choose the region your data is stored in, or run the platform on your own infrastructure.
Priority support Priority routing and response-time commitments on support requests.
